calls.head: Don’t expect many shots
calls.body: Philadelphia’s games average only 77.5 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (31st of 32 for pace); Ottawa’s average 79.3 (25th).
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 77.1 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 78.4 and a league average of 81.5.

calls.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
calls.body: Philadelphia’s hit score is 111 (6th of 32) and Ottawa’s is 122 (2nd). 100 is league average, after adjusting for each arena’s scorer.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 110, against their usual 116 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 67% chance, and Ottawa delivered.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 33% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Ottawa won without the better chances
surprises.body: Expected goals favoured Philadelphia, 3.3 to 2.3, with empty nets left out. L. Ullmark stopped 2.3 more goals than expected.

surprises.head: Philadelphia shot far more than usual
surprises.body: 66.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, adjusted for score and venue, against its usual 46.0.

surprises.head: Philadelphia tried a different line
surprises.body: C. Dvorak, O. Tippett, T. Zegras played 8:21 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Philadelphia’s usual lines.
